name: Linked trace projection (one motion, two representations)

source.description: 1 inspected reference film (batch-4, 2026-11-26): a maths reel turns a point on the unit circle while a guide line carries its height across to draw a sine wave.

technique: A point moves on one figure (a circle, a rotating arm) while a guide line carries one of its coordinates across to an adjacent axis, where it draws a curve over time. The viewer sees that the circle and the wave are one motion, which a static diagram cannot show.
purpose: Show that two representations are one motion (a circle and a wave, a mechanism and its graph), which a static diagram cannot.
visual_behaviour: A point turns on a circle with its radius and angle arc; a guide line carries one coordinate across to an axis, where a curve draws itself in step.
mechanics: Point angle = 2*pi*t/T with linear ease; guide line from the point to x = x0 + k*t on the graph at the same height; the curve is a path drawn by stroke-dashoffset (or a growing polyline) up to the guide line's end; a radius line and an angle arc on the circle; T = 1.5-3 s per cycle; both driven from the same timeline variable.

decomposition.timing: One cycle in 1.5-3 s; 1-2 cycles per explanation beat (reference 2-4 s).

use_cases: Sine and cosine from the unit circle
Any mapping from a mechanism to its graph (piston to pressure, orbit to brightness)
failure_modes: Point and curve drifting apart: compute both from one time variable

implementation.approach: Studio.comp.tracePair(parent, {cycles, period}) (runtime 1.18.0): one proxy angle sets the radius, point, angle arc, level guide line, graph point and the clip that reveals the pre-drawn sine path, so the two views cannot drift apart; run() turns it linearly at period seconds per turn.

provenance.observed: A point turns on the unit circle while a guide line carries its height across to draw a pink sine wave on the right (2-4 s).

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).

evidence.notes: 0 errors, 0 warnings; contact sheet inspected on Windows (Playwright preview, not a HyperFrames render).
